replies.content: There are some holes right next to others on the corners. Make sure you are doing the right ones. I did this a couple tries before realizing I wasn't putting them on the one's all the way on the corners.

content:
Expansion joint screws were not called out in the last section. Don't use the old ones. There is a bag with new silver ones.

Also I found it easier to finger tighten these until you put the expansion joints on.
Use a 2.0 mm Allen key here
I put the washers on the screw upside down first and then put the screws in
Don’t fully tighten, it’s too difficult to install the expansion joints in the next step and risk damaging washers.
Beware that if the washers aren't perfectly centered around the screw post, it might bind against the ridge on the screw and fool you into thinking it's fully tightened.
Tighten fully, but do not overtighten – but then leave a gap, so that it isn't actually fully tightened? That could be clearer.

replies.content: Yes this had me confused too!
Hello. You're right, the sentence was worded incorrectly. We have now corrected the instruction.
